rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God subjected the east wind to Sulayman.
rows.anchor: وسخرنا له الريح وهي الصبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its morning course ran from sunrise to noon and covered a month's journey at the pace of ordinary mounts.
rows.anchor: جريها وسيرها بالغداة أي : من لدن طلوع الشمس إلى زوالها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its evening course ran from noon until night for another month's journey, so a rider covered two months' distance in one day.
rows.anchor: جريها وسيرها بالعشي أي : من انتصاف النهار إلى الليل

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib defines a month by the sighting of the new moon or as one twelfth of the sun's circuit.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب : الشهر مدة معروفة مشهورة بإهلال الهلال أو باعتبار جزء من اثني عشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about the wind's morning and evening journeys can be an independent sentence or a circumstantial clause modifying the wind.
rows.anchor: والجملة إما مستأنفة أو حال من الريح

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says Sulayman left Damascus at dawn, rested at Asṭakhr at noon, then traveled to Kabul; he also took meals at Ray and Samarqand.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن كان يغدو بدمشق مع جنوده على البساط فيقيل باصطخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asṭakhr was a Persian town built for Sulayman by the jinn Sakhr, whom the author identifies with the ifrit in 27:39.
rows.anchor: واصطخر بوزن فردوس بلدة من بلاد فارس بناها لسليمان صخر الجني المراد بقوله : {قال عفريت من الجن}

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: An inscription seen at a Tigris-side house, attributed to Sulayman's companions, said they had found the house built and traveled from Asṭakhr toward Syria.
rows.anchor: ويحكى أن بعضهم رأى مكتوبا في منزل بناحية دجلة كتبه بعض أصحاب سليمان

rows.speaker: كشف الأسرار
rows.claim: Kashf al-Asrar gives Sulayman's route through Iraq, Marv, Balkh, Turkish lands, Qandahar, Makran, and Kerman to Asṭakhr, then says he reached Tadmor from there in a day.
rows.anchor: قال في "كشف الأسرار" : (كفته اند سفروى از زمين عراق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before leaving Syria for Iraq, Sulayman ordered the demons to build for him with stone slabs, columns, and white and yellow marble; verses were found engraved on a Syrian rock.
rows.anchor: وكان سليمان أمر الشياطين قبل شخوصه من الشام إلى العراق فبنوها له بالصفاح والعمد والرخام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A responsible person should worship and fear God rather than defy Him, and should not be worse than inanimate things despite being creation's noblest kind.
rows.anchor: فينبغي للعاقل المكلف أن يعبد الله ويخافه ولا يجترىء على ما يخالف رضاه

rows.speaker: جعفر الطيار
rows.claim: Ja'far al-Tayyar recounts that the Prophet asked a mountain to greet him and provide water; the mountain replied that fear of 2:24 had made it weep until its water was gone.
rows.anchor: قال جعفر الطيار رضي الله عنه : كنت مع النبي عليه السلام وكان حذاءنا جبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author gives two verb forms: wazara-yaziru, with the verbal noun wazr, and wazara-yūzaru, meaning to carry.
rows.anchor: يقال وزر يزر من الثاني وزرا بالفتح والكسر ووزر يوزر من الرابع حمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wizr means sin and burden; wāzira and ukhrā describe an omitted feminine soul, so the sense is that no sinful soul bears another's guilt at resurrection.
rows.anchor: والوزر الإثم والثقل والوازرة صفة للنفس المحذوفة وكذا أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each soul bears the sins it acquired; in worldly life, by contrast, tyrants may punish one ally or neighbor for another.
rows.anchor: لا تحمل نفس آثمة يوم القيامة إثم نفس أخرى بحيث تتعرى منه المحمول عنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The extra loads in 29:13 are the deceivers' own sins of misguidance and leading others astray, not the victims' sins; 29:12's promise to bear others' errors is expressly denied.
rows.anchor: فهو حمل أثقال ضلالهم مع أثقال إضلالهم وكلاهما أوزارهم ليس فيها شيء من أوزار غيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When oppressors are charged with victims' sins, the charge is actually recompense for their transgressive oppression, though it appears to lighten the victim's load.
rows.anchor: فإن المحمول في الحقيقة جزاء الظلم وإن كان يحصل في الظاهر تخفيف حمل المظلوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each creature has a particular secret and relation with God and is accountable for its own endowment, just as each seed grows only the plant stored within it; Bursevī cites al-Ta'wilat al-Najmiyya.
rows.anchor: أن الله تعالى في خلق كل واحد من الخلق سرا مخصوصا به وله مع كل واحد شأن آخر

rows.speaker: سعدي
rows.claim: Saadi's couplet reinforces the image that each seed bears only its own kind of fruit.
rows.anchor: رطب ناورد وب خر زهره بار ه تخم افيكنى بر همان شم دار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb is feminine singular and means if she calls, with the soul understood as its subject.
rows.anchor: صيغة غائبة أي : ولو دعت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The burdened one is a soul weighed down by sins; the object of her appeal is omitted and understood as another person.
rows.anchor: أي : نفس أثقلتها الأوزار والمفعول محذوف أي : أحدا

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib says heaviness and lightness are opposites: the term began with physical weight and extends metaphorically to debts and sins.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب : الثقل والخفة متقابلان وكل ما يترجح عما يوزن به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sin is called a weight because it burdens its bearer on judgment day and holds the sinner back from reward in this life.
rows.anchor: فالثقل الإثم سمي به لأنه يثقل صاحبه يوم القيامة ويثبطه عن الثواب في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The appeal is for someone to carry some of the sins already resting on the burdened soul.
rows.anchor: الذي عليها من الذنوب ليحمل بعضها

rows.speaker: المفردات
rows.claim: Al-Mufradat distinguishes ḥiml, with kasra, for an external load from ḥaml, with fatha, for an internal burden such as a child in the womb.
rows.anchor: حمل بالفتح كما في "المفردات"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person asked does not agree to carry any part of the sins.
rows.anchor: لم تجب لحمل شيء منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wa-law is connective here; kāna refers to the omitted person addressed in the appeal, making the statement cover every possible helper.
rows.anchor: {ولو} للوصل {كان} أي : المدعو المفهوم من الدعوة وترك ذكره ليشمل كل مدعو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even a close relative of the caller, such as a parent, child, or sibling, cannot help, since each person is overwhelmed by their own concern and load.
rows.anchor: ذا قرابة من الداعي كالأب والأم والولد والأخ ونحو ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse shows that God holds only the sinner accountable and that appealing to relatives cannot avail those who lack piety.
rows.anchor: ففي هذا دليل أنه تعالى لا يؤاخذ بالذنب إلا جانيه وأن الاستغاثة بالأقربين غير نافعة لغير المتقين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that on judgment day parents ask their child to carry some sins, but the child refuses; a husband similarly asks his wife for even a speck of good, and she says she fears for herself.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما يلقى الأب والأم ابنه فيقول يا بني احمل عني بعض ذنوبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unattributed Persian couplet says kinship and friendship cannot save a person from the reckoning when everyone is preoccupied with their own fate.
rows.anchor: هي رحمى نه برادر به برادر دارد

rows.speaker: الإرشاد
rows.claim: Al-Irshad distinguishes the clauses: the current one denies voluntary burden-bearing, while the preceding clause denies being made to bear another's sin by force.
rows.anchor: قال في "الإرشاد" : هذه الآية نفي للتحمل اختيارا والأولى نفي له إجبارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Obedience is light and disobedience darkness; neither quality transfers between people, and at the crossing each walks by their own light without another's light passing to them.
rows.anchor: أن الطاعة نور والعصيان ظلمة فإذا اتصف جوهر الإنسان بصفة النور أو بصفة الظلمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Warning is communicating a message together with causing fear.
rows.anchor: والإنذار الإبلاغ مع التخويف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The addressees are those who fear their Lord while unseen, either because punishment and the afterlife's rulings are unseen to them or because they fear privately, away from people.
rows.anchor: غائبين عن عذابه وأحكام الآخرة أو عن الناس في خلواتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the first reading, the phrase is circumstantial of the object; on the private-devotion reading, it is circumstantial of the subject who fears.
rows.anchor: فهو حال من الفاعل أو حال كون ذلك العذاب غائبا عنهم فهو حال من المفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They observe prayer as it should be observed, making it a raised beacon and an upright standard.
rows.anchor: راعوها كما ينبغي وجعلوها منارا منصوبا وعلما مرفوعا

rows.speaker: كشف الأسرار
rows.claim: Kashf al-Asrar explains the varied wording by noting that fear is continuous, whereas prayer times are fixed and pass.
rows.anchor: قال في "كشف الأسرار" وغاير بين اللفظين لأن أوقات الخشية دائمة وأوقات الصلاة معينة منقضية

words: إنما تنذر الذين يخشون ربهم بالغيب
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning benefits these people, though the Prophet warns everyone; fear and prayer are singled out as roots of inward and outward good deeds, prayer being religion's pillar and fear a sign of certainty.
rows.anchor: والمعنى إنما ينفع إنذارك وتحذيرك هؤلاء من قومك دون من عداهم من أهل التمرد والفساد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fear of God rises with knowledge of Him, as 35:28 says; a heart without knowledge and fear is dead and unmoved by warning, as 36:70 describes the living recipient.
rows.anchor: كما قال تعالى : {ومن الناس والدوآب والانعام مختلف ألوانه}

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A hadith says that abandoning prayer stands between a person and polytheism and unbelief.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث "إن بين الرجل وبين الشرك والكفر ترك الصلاة"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person purified has shed sins and disobedience by responding to these warnings and has repaired their state through acts of obedience.
rows.anchor: تطهر من أوضار الأوزار والمعاصي بالتأثر من هذه الإنذارات وأصلح حاله بفعل الطاعات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Purification benefits only its practitioner, just as sin's stain harms only its bearer; one who gives alms also earns its reward for oneself.
rows.anchor: لاقتصار نفعه عليها كما أن من تدنس بها لا يتدنس إلا عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All return is to God alone, who rewards purification; purification from sin earns Paradise and its degrees, while release from attachment to all besides God earns His beauty.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن ثواب التزكي عن المعاصي هو الجنة ودرجاتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One who freely returns to God finds no lasting repose in anything below Him.
rows.anchor: فمن رجع إلى الله بالاختيار لم يبق له بما دونه قرار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The living and dead are another, stronger image for believers and unbelievers: the repeated verb and plural forms stress their contrast, and believers use life for remembrance outwardly and reflection inwardly.
rows.anchor: تمثيل آخر للمؤمنين والكافرين أبلغ من الأول ولذلك كرر الفعل وأوثرت صيغة الجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here the living is what possesses sensory power, while the dead is what has lost it; the unbeliever's outward conduct is idle and inward state false.
rows.anchor: والحي ما به القوة الحساسة

rows.speaker: بعض العلماء
rows.claim: Some scholars take the image as scholars versus the ignorant, since likening ignorant people to the dead is familiar; a cited couplet calls the ignorant a dead person in a shroud.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض العلماء : هو تمثيل للعلماء والجهال وتشبيه الجهلة بالأموات شائع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: True life belongs to spirits and hearts through wisdom and knowledge of realities; bodily life alone has no special value because animals share it.
rows.anchor: لأن الحياة المعتبرة هي حياة الأرواح والقلوب وذلك بالحكم والمعارف ولا عبرة بحياة الأجساد

rows.speaker: بعض الكبار
rows.claim: Some Sufi masters say the truly living are those who attain real life through total annihilation, dying voluntarily before death by effacing their acts, attributes, and selves in God's.
rows.anchor: قال بعض الكبار : الأحياء عند التحقيق هم الواصلون بالفناء التام إلى الحياة الحقيقية

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet is quoted as saying that whoever wants to see a moving dead person should look at Abu Bakr, illustrating the Sufi language of voluntary death.
rows.anchor: وإليه الإشارة بقوله عليه السلام : "من أراد أن ينظر إلى ميت متحرك فلينظر إلى أبي بكر"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Spiritual life endures, unlike bodily life, which ends with death; felicity belongs to those with lasting life and their companions and disciples.
rows.anchor: فالحياة المعنوية لا يطرأ عليها الفناء بخلاف الحياة الصورية فإنها تزول بالموت

rows.speaker: أبو يزيد
rows.claim: Ibrahim al-Harawi recounts Abu Yazid saying that ordinary people take knowledge from the dead, while his group takes divinely inspired knowledge from the Ever-Living without study or effort.
rows.anchor: قال إبراهيم الهروي : كنت بمجلس أبي يزيد البسطامي قدس سره فقال بعضهم : إن فلانا أخذ العلم

rows.speaker: سعدي
rows.claim: Saadi's lines say that people are more than bones and outward forms, and that not every form contains a living soul and meaning.
rows.anchor: نه مردم همين استخوانند ويوسف نه هر صورتى جان ومعنى دروست

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God makes the person He wills hear with understanding and heedfulness by reviving the heart, so that the person benefits from the warning.
rows.anchor: كلامه إسماع فهم واتعاظ وذلك بإحياء القلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qabr means the place where a dead person is laid, and qabar-tu means I placed him in the grave.
rows.anchor: جمع قبر وهو مقر الميت وقبرته جعلته في القبر

words: وما أنت بمسمع من في القبور
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The grave image extends the comparison: just as the buried cannot hear or answer, people sealed in unbelief cannot hear or accept truth; it further discourages the Prophet from expecting their conversion.
rows.anchor: وهذا الكلام ترشيح لتمثيل المصرين على الكفر بالأموات وإشباع في إقناطه عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's office is to warn of fire and punishment; making sealed hearts hear is God's work and beyond the Prophet's power.
rows.anchor: منذر بالنار والعقاب وأما الإسماع البتة فليس من وظائفك ولا حيلة لك إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Together with 28:56 and 3:128, this wording distinguishes God's station from the Prophet's so the community will not confuse them as earlier peoples did when they called Ezra or Jesus God's son.
rows.anchor: وقوله : {إن الله يسمع} الخ وقوله : {إنك لا تهدى من أحببت

words: وما أنت بمسمع من في القبور
rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: At Badr the Prophet addressed the dead in the well, asking whether they found God's promise true; he said they heard his words no less than the living, though they could not answer.
rows.anchor: فقال عليه السلام : "ما أنتم بأسمع لما أقول منهم غير أنهم لا يستطيعون أن يردوا شيئا"

words: وما أنت بمسمع من في القبور
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevī reconciles the Badr report by suggesting God revived the well's dead to hear the Prophet as humiliation and regret; a dead person as such does not hear.
rows.anchor: قلت : أما الأول فيحتمل أن الله تعالى أحيى أهل القليب حينئذ حتى سمعوا كلام رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The saying that the dead heard no less than the living indicates that spirits hear better than bodies with souls, because the veil of sense is removed and rent.
rows.anchor: يدل على أن الأرواح أسمع من الأجساد مع الأرواح لزوال حجاب الحس وانخراقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question is confirmatory, and seeing means knowing with the heart; it addresses Muhammad or anyone fit to receive the address.
rows.anchor: الاستفهام تفريري والرؤية قلبية أي : ألم تعلم يعني قد علمت يا محمد أو يا من يليق به الخطاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky can mean the upper direction or a cloud, and the water is rain.
rows.anchor: من الجهة العلوية سماء أو سحابا {مآء} مطرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift from third-person reference to God's first-person plural highlights the wondrous act of bringing forth, its power and wisdom, and gives the expression greater majesty.
rows.anchor: والالتفات من الغيبة إلى التكلم لإظهار كمال الاعتناء بفعل الإخراج لما فيه من الصنع البديع

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Al-Kashifi explains the first-person shift as specifying the act: We are the ones who bring things out by that water.
rows.anchor: وقال الكاشفي : (عدول متكلم جهت تخصيص فعل است يعني ماتوانييم كه بيرون آريم بدان آب)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thamarah is a general name for anything edible produced by trees.
rows.anchor: جمع ثمرة وهي اسم لكل ما يطعم من أحمال الشجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may distinguish kinds of fruit, such as pomegranates, apples, figs, and grapes, or cultivars within a kind, including over fifty grape varieties and over a hundred dates.
rows.anchor: أجناسها من الرمان والتفاح والتين والعنب وغيرها أو أصنافها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It may also describe fruits' visible forms and colors, including yellow, red, green, white, and black.
rows.anchor: أو هيآتها من الصفرة والحمرة والخضرة والبياض والسواد وغيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Judad is the subject and predicate construction; because the ridges themselves cannot be said to come from mountains, an omitted phrase is supplied: some mountains have colored ridges.
rows.anchor: {ومن الجبال جدد} مبتدأ وخبر

rows.speaker: المفردات
rows.claim: Al-Mufradat glosses judad as visible paths, from the expression for a traversed, cut-out road and the word for a main road.
rows.anchor: في "المفردات" أي : طرائق ظاهرة من قولهم طريق مجدود أي : مسلوك مقطوع ومنه جادة الطريق

rows.speaker: الجلالين
rows.claim: Al-Jalalayn understands the mountain ridges as paths that resemble veins running through mountains.
rows.anchor: في "الجلالين" الطرائق تكون في الجبال كالعروق

rows.speaker: كشف الأسرار
rows.claim: Kashf al-Asrar reads the ridges as paths revealed in the mountains, with white and red tracks on differently colored mountains.
rows.anchor: وفي"كشف الأسرار" : (واز كوهها راهها بيدا شده از روندكان خطها سبد وخطها سرخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevī prefers naturally occurring colored bands in the mountains over traveled paths, because the passage describes created features and the ridges' colors may differ from the mountain's own color.
rows.anchor: والظاهر هو الأول لأن المقام لبيان ما هو خلقي على أن كون الطريقة بيضاء لا يستلزم كون الجبال كذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bayḍ and ḥumr are plural adjectives describing the ridges as white and red.
rows.anchor: {بيض} جمع أبيض صفة جدد {وحمر} جمع أحمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The middle mountain example parallels the preceding fruit colors and following human and animal colors, requiring the omitted phrase so all three clauses describe differing colors.
rows.anchor: فتلا عليه السلام القرائن الثلاث فإن ما قبلها فأخرجنا به ثمرات مختلفا ألوانها وما بعدها ومن الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The colors belong to the ridges; even whites vary in intensity from one to another, as do reds, making each color a graded universal.
rows.anchor: ألوان تلك الجدد إلا أن قوله مختلف ألوانها صفة لكل واحدة من الجدد البيض والحمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevī parses the wording as an implicit black followed by its explanation, estimated as سود غرابيب سود; repetition reinforces it, and he prefers this to the majority's analysis of سود as a delayed substitute.
rows.anchor: قلت : الغرابيب تأكيد لمضمر يفسره ما بعده والتقدير سود غرابيب سود

rows.speaker: الأكثر
rows.claim: Most grammarians, including the author of al-Qamus, treat سود as a substitute for غرابيب; Bursevī objects that color emphasis cannot precede the emphasized word.
rows.anchor: وهذا أصوب من كون السود بدلا من الغرابيب كما ذهب إليه الأكثر حتى صاحب "القاموس"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dawabb are animals that move on the earth, though the word commonly refers to riding animals such as horses, mules, and donkeys, and it can be masculine.
rows.anchor: جمع دابة وهي ما يدب على الأرض من الحيوان وغلب على ما يركب من الخيل والبغال والحمير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An'am means camels, cattle, sheep, and goats; horses, mules, and donkeys are excluded.
rows.anchor: جمع نعم محركة وقد يسكن عينه الإبل والبقر والضأن والمعز دون غيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular pronoun in مختلف ألوانه refers to an implicit some drawn from من; some people and animals vary as white, red, or black.
rows.anchor: بأن يكون أبيض وأحمر وأسود ولم يقل هنا ألوانها لأن الضمير يعود إلى البعض الدال عليه من

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kadhālika is a simile-forming verbal noun modifying an implied مصدر of اختلاف, and it closes the preceding clause.
rows.anchor: تم الكلام هنا وهو مصدر تشبيهي لقوله مختلف أي : صفة لمصدر مؤكد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One who fails to recognize God's power to create things and transform them from state to state will not fear Him.
rows.anchor: هركه نداند قدرت خدايرا بر آفريدن اشيا وعالم نبود بتحويل هر يزى از حالى بحالى كونه از خداى تعالى ترسد

words: إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء
rows.speaker: الإرشاد
rows.claim: Al-Irshad links this to 35:18, identifying those who truly fear God as people who know Him and His attributes and acts; fear depends on knowledge, and the Prophet said he was most God-fearing.
rows.anchor: وفي "الإرشاد" وهو تكملة لقوله تعالى : {إنما تنذر الذين يخشون ربهم بالغيب}

words: إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء
rows.speaker: الإرشاد
rows.claim: Al-Irshad explains that those deprived of knowledge of God, including the unbelievers, cannot be affected by warning; the following mention of God's acts demonstrates His power.
rows.anchor: وحيث كان الكفرة بمعزل عن هذه المعرفة امتنع إنذارهم بالكلية انتهى

words: إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Putting God, the object of fear, before العلماء restricts who fears Him to the learned; reversing the order would instead mean that they fear no one but God.
rows.anchor: وتقديم المخشي وهو المفعول للاختصاص وحصر الفاعلية أي : لا يخشى الله من بين عباده إلا العلماء

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة وعمر بن عبد العزيز وابن سيرين
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa, Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, and Ibn Sirin read Allah in the nominative and العلماء in the accusative, using fear metaphorically for honoring: God honors the learned.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو حنيفة وعمر بن عبد العزيز وابن سيرين برفع اسم الله ونصب العلماء

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
rows.claim: Abd Allah ibn Umar takes khashya here to mean choosing, so God chooses the learned from among His servants.
rows.anchor: وجعل عبد الله بن عمر الخشية بمعنى الاختيار أي : إنما يختار الله من بين عباده العلماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is mighty in exacting vengeance from one who does not fear His punishment, and forgiving toward those who fear Him; these attributes explain why He must be feared.
rows.anchor: غالبست در انتقام كشيدن از كسى كه نترسد از عقوبت او

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fear is heartache at an expected future harm, arising either from many sins or from knowledge of God's majesty; prophetic fear belongs to the latter kind.
rows.anchor: قيل الخشية تألم القلب بسبب توقع مكروه في المستقبل يكون تارة بكثرة الجناية من العبد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers should seek knowledge of God, since degrees of fear and reverent awe rise in proportion to knowledge.
rows.anchor: فعلى المؤمن أن يجتهد في تحصيل العلم بالله حتى يكون أخشى الناس فبقدر مراتب العلم تكون مراتب الخوف والخشية

words: إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء
rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: In a report attributed to the Prophet, the most knowledgeable person is the one most fearful of God; the best companion helps remembrance, the worst neither helps nor reminds, and a corrupt scholar corrupts people.
rows.anchor: روي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه سئل يا رسول الله أينا أعلم؟ قال : "أخشاكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing Persian couplet warns that reading more without putting knowledge into practice leaves a person ignorant.
rows.anchor: علم جندانكه بيشتر خوانى ون عمل در تونيست نادانى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevī prays to be made knowledgeable and realized, and sincere in fear and reverent awe.
rows.anchor: نسأل الله سبحانه أن يجعلنا عالمين ومحققين وفي الخوف والخشية صادقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They recite the Qur'an continually and act on it, since recitation without practice has no benefit; recitation can include study and regular litanies, but not spelling out words for instruction.
rows.anchor: يداومون على تلاوة القرآن ويعملون بما فيه إذ لا تنفع التلاوة بدون العمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because spelling out Qur'anic letters is not counted as recitation, a person in major ritual impurity or menstruation may spell it out or teach it word by word with pauses.
rows.anchor: لا يكره التهجي للجنب والحائض والنفساء بالقرآن لأنه لا يعد قارئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The present tense for recitation contrasts with the past for prayer because recitation times extend, while prayer times are fixed and pass; the same contrast applies to spending as an allusion to zakat.
rows.anchor: وغاير بين المستقبل والماضي لأن أوقات التلاوة أعم بخلاف أوقات الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They spend from what God has given them in charitable and other good causes.
rows.anchor: في وجوه البر يعني : (ازدست بيرون كنند درويشانرا)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase can describe giving secretly and publicly, secret and public charity, or donors who act privately and openly; the words are more often used of meanings than physical objects.
rows.anchor: وهي ضد السر وأكثر ما يقال ذلك في المعاني دون الأعيان يقال أعلنته فعلن

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Al-Kashifi says secret charity avoids ostentation and public charity encourages others; Bursevī identifies the former as recommended and the latter as obligatory, and sees both as inner and outer knowledge.
rows.anchor: وقال الكاشفي : {سرا} (

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning both forms encourages spending for God in all times and circumstances.
rows.anchor: وفيه بعث للمنفق على الصدقة في سبيل الله في عموم الأوقات والأحوال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yarjūna is the predicate of inna.
rows.anchor: يرجون} خبر إن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The enduring trade is the reward gained through obedience; trade is the use of capital to seek profit, and b-w-r means extreme stagnation or loss.
rows.anchor: تحصيل ثواب بالطاعة والتاجر الذي يبيع ويشتري وعمله التجارة وهي التصرف في رأس المال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author notes that Arabic has no other word with tā followed by jīm besides tijāra; tijāh and tajawwub have different origins or use tā as a prefix.
rows.anchor: قيل : وليس في كلامهم تاء بعدها جيم غير هذه اللفظة وأما تجاه فأصله وجاه
